MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #1
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which Roman numeral stands for 9? (1 mark)
   A. IIII
   B. VIIII
   C. VX
   D. IX

2. Which of these is a factor of 50? (1 mark)
   A. 4
   B. 25
   C. 3
   D. 6

3. How many factors does 50 have? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 8
   C. 5
   D. 6

4. Which of these shows 305 in words? (1 mark)
   A. four hundred and five
   B. thirty-five
   C. three hundred and fifty
   D. three hundred and five

5. How many factors does 20 have? (1 mark)
   A. 6
   B. 7
   C. 8
   D. 5

6. Work out 2,450 + 3,875. (1 mark)
   A. 6,225
   B. 6,325
   C. 5,225
   D. 6,335

7. Work out 2,345 + 1,432. (1 mark)
   A. 3,787
   B. 4,777
   C. 3,677
   D. 3,777

8. Work out 3,999 + 4,001. (1 mark)
   A. 8,000
   B. 8,010
   C. 7,990
   D. 7,900

9. Njeri had Ksh 5,000 and bought a bag for Ksh 1,850. How much money does she have left? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 4,850
   B. Ksh 3,150
   C. Ksh 3,250
   D. Ksh 3,140

10. Work out 4,000 − 1,236. (1 mark)
   A. 2,764
   B. 3,236
   C. 2,774
   D. 2,664

11. In 5,432 − 2,718, the ones digit 2 is smaller than 8. From which digit do we borrow? (1 mark)
   A. We swap the 2 and the 8
   B. The hundreds digit 4, which becomes 3
   C. The tens digit 3, which becomes 2
   D. The thousands digit 5, which becomes 4

12. Work out 27 × 13. (1 mark)
   A. 351
   B. 361
   C. 108
   D. 341

13. A trader buys 18 crates with 35 bananas in each crate. How many bananas are there? (1 mark)
   A. 630 bananas
   B. 610 bananas
   C. 620 bananas
   D. 730 bananas

14. A remainder must always be (1 mark)
   A. bigger than the divisor
   B. smaller than the divisor
   C. equal to the divisor
   D. equal to the quotient

15. 38 eggs are packed in trays that each hold 5 eggs. How many trays are needed to pack all the eggs? (1 mark)
   A. 6
   B. 9
   C. 7
   D. 8

16. A circle is cut into 12 equal parts and 5 parts are shaded. What fraction is not shaded? (1 mark)
   A. 7/5
   B. 5/12
   C. 7/12
   D. 12/7

17. In the fraction 7/8, what does the numerator 7 tell us? (1 mark)
   A. How many equal parts the whole has
   B. The number of wholes
   C. The size of each part in centimetres
   D. How many of the equal parts are taken

18. Change 13/3 to a mixed fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 1 4/3
   B. 4 1/3
   C. 4 2/3
   D. 5 1/3

19. Dan writes another set of fractions. Which of these is a mixed fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 8/3
   B. 11/5
   C. 1/2
   D. 4 2/3

20. A hundred square has 82 of its small squares shaded. Which decimal shows the shaded part? (1 mark)
   A. 0.82
   B. 8.2
   C. 0.082
   D. 82

21. Write 0.09 as a fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 90/100
   B. 9/1000
   C. 9/100
   D. 9/10

22. Write 0.37 as a fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 3/7
   B. 37/10
   C. 37/100
   D. 37/1000

23. Ksh 12.50 means (1 mark)
   A. 125 shillings
   B. 12 shillings and 5 cents
   C. 1 shilling and 250 cents
   D. 12 shillings and 50 cents

24. Simplify 2a + 5 + 3a + 1. (1 mark)
   A. 6a + 5
   B. 11a
   C. 5a + 6
   D. 5a + 5

25. Simplify 8y + 2 − 3y. (1 mark)
   A. 5y + 2
   B. 5y − 2
   C. 11y + 2
   D. 7y

26. A square has sides of 9 cm. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 18 cm
   B. 36 cm
   C. 27 cm
   D. 81 cm

27. What is 3 m 45 cm + 2 m 80 cm? (1 mark)
   A. 6 m 15 cm
   B. 5 m 25 cm
   C. 7 m 25 cm
   D. 6 m 25 cm

28. A rectangle has 5 rows and 8 columns. How many small squares are needed to cover it? (1 mark)
   A. 45
   B. 26
   C. 40
   D. 13

29. A square is covered with 3 rows of 3 unit squares. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 6 square units
   B. 9 square units
   C. 8 square units
   D. 12 square units

30. How can you compare the areas of two sheets of paper without measuring? (1 mark)
   A. Count the number of corners
   B. Put one on top of the other and see which one sticks out
   C. Measure their masses
   D. Fold both into halves and count folds only

31. A cuboid is 5 blocks long, 5 blocks wide and 5 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 130 blocks
   B. 15 blocks
   C. 25 blocks
   D. 125 blocks

32. A stack of soda crates has 5 crates along a wall, 4 crates deep and 4 layers high. How many crates are in the stack? (1 mark)
   A. 20 crates
   B. 80 crates
   C. 100 crates
   D. 13 crates

33. On an analogue clock the short hour hand has reached or passed the number 7 but not yet reached the next number, and the long minute hand points to the number 9. What time is shown? (1 mark)
   A. 7:45
   B. 7:09
   C. 8:45
   D. 7:15

34. 1,250 cents is the same as (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 1.25
   B. Ksh 125
   C. Ksh 13.50
   D. Ksh 12.50

35. Which is the same as half a shilling? (1 mark)
   A. 50 cents
   B. 10 cents
   C. 500 cents
   D. 5 cents

36. One unit costs Ksh 65. What is the cost of 3 exercise books? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 130
   B. Ksh 68
   C. Ksh 205
   D. Ksh 195

37. Kip faces West and makes a quarter turn clockwise. Which way does he face now? (1 mark)
   A. West
   B. North
   C. South
   D. East

38. Which sign is used to mark a right angle in a drawing? (1 mark)
   A. A wavy line
   B. A small circle
   C. A small triangle
   D. A small square in the corner

39. The table shows the favourite sports of 10 pupils: football 5, netball 3, athletics 1, swimming 1. How many are NOT swimming? (1 mark)
   A. 9
   B. 10
   C. 1
   D. 11

40. Why do we add up the totals in a table? (1 mark)
   A. To hide the data
   B. To make the table longer
   C. To change the data
   D. To check that the numbers are correct

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Add 3 m 45 cm and 2 m 80 cm. (3 marks)

42. Add 2 1/2 kg and 1 3/4 kg. Show your working. (3 marks)

43. Amina faces north. She makes a half turn, then a quarter turn anticlockwise. Which way does she face at the end? (4 marks)

44. Mr Otieno has Ksh 2,000. He buys items costing Ksh 1,340. Does he have enough money? How much is left? (3 marks)

45. Explain why 2a + 3b cannot be written as 5ab. (2 marks)

46. Why can we not tell the mass of an object only by looking at its size? Give an example. (3 marks)

47. Subtract 2,718 from 5,432, showing every regrouping step. (4 marks)

48. School starts at 8:00 a.m. and ends at 3:15 p.m. Lunch is from 12:40 p.m. to 1:40 p.m. (a) How long is the school day? (b) How long is it from the start of school to the start of lunch? (c) How long is it from the end of lunch to the end of school? (5 marks)

49. Work out 4 L − 1 3/4 L. Show your working. (3 marks)

50. Wanjiku has 2 L of milk and buys 1 1/2 L more. How much milk does she have now? (2 marks)

51. Njeri faces east. She makes two quarter turns clockwise, one after the other. Which way does she face? (3 marks)

52. Arrange these prices from the cheapest to the most expensive: Ksh 8.25, Ksh 8.05, Ksh 8.50, Ksh 7.99. (3 marks)

53. A farmer joins 4 pieces of wire, each measuring 2 m 30 cm, to make one long wire. Find the length of the long wire. (3 marks)

54. Write 0.7, 0.07, 0.75 and 0.57 in order from the smallest to the largest. (3 marks)

55. Explain how you would find the lines of symmetry of a paper rectangle. How many are there? (4 marks)

56. A jerrycan holds 5 L. Musa pours out 2 1/2 L. How much is left in the jerrycan? (2 marks)

57. Wanjiru saves Ksh 250 every week. Write how much she has saved after 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 weeks. State the rule. (3 marks)

58. The mass of a basket full of mangoes is 8 kg and the basket alone is 1 1/2 kg. Find the mass of the mangoes alone. (2 marks)

59. Ten pupils were asked their favourite fruit and the answers were: mango, banana, mango, orange, banana, mango, pawpaw, mango, banana, orange. (a) Show the data in a tally table. (b) Which fruit is the most popular? (c) How many more pupils chose mango than orange? (5 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #1 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — IX
   9 is written IX. I before X is 10 − 1.

2. B — 25
   50 ÷ 25 = 2 with nothing left over, so 25 is a factor of 50. The others leave a remainder.

3. D — 6
   The factors of 50 are 1, 2, 5, 10, 25, 50. There are 6 of them.

4. D — three hundred and five
   305 = three hundred and five. Say the hundreds, then "and", then the tens and ones.

5. A — 6
   The factors of 20 are 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20. There are 6 of them.

6. B — 6,325
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 2,450 + 3,875 = 6,325.

7. D — 3,777
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 2,345 + 1,432 = 3,777.

8. A — 8,000
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 3,999 + 4,001 = 8,000.

9. B — Ksh 3,150
   Subtract 5,000 − 1,850 = 3,150. Check by adding: 3,150 + 1,850 = 5,000.

10. A — 2,764
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 4,000 − 1,236 = 2,764. Check: 2,764 + 1,236 = 4,000.

11. C — The tens digit 3, which becomes 2
   Borrow one ten from the tens column. The 3 becomes 2 and the ones digit 2 becomes 12.

12. A — 351
   27 × 3 = 81 and 27 × 10 = 270. 81 + 270 = 351.

13. A — 630 bananas
   Multiply to find the total. The answer is 630 bananas.

14. B — smaller than the divisor
   If the remainder were as big as the divisor, another whole group could still be made.

15. D — 8
   38 ÷ 5 = 7 remainder 3. The 3 left-over eggs need one more tray, so 8 trays are needed.

16. C — 7/12
   Not shaded: 12 − 5 = 7 parts, so 7/12.

17. D — How many of the equal parts are taken
   The numerator is the top number. In 7/8 it says that 7 parts are taken.

18. B — 4 1/3
   13 ÷ 3 = 4 remainder 1. The whole number is 4 and the fraction is 1/3, so 13/3 = 4 1/3.

19. D — 4 2/3
   A mixed fraction has a whole number and a proper fraction, like 4 2/3.

20. A — 0.82
   82 out of 100 squares is 82/100 = 0.82.

21. C — 9/100
   The last digit of 0.09 is in the hundredths place, so the denominator is 100. 0.09 = 9/100.

22. C — 37/100
   The last digit of 0.37 is in the hundredths place, so the denominator is 100. 0.37 = 37/100.

23. D — 12 shillings and 50 cents
   The digits after the decimal point are the cents. Ksh 12.50 is 12 shillings and 50 cents.

24. C — 5a + 6
   Only like terms can be joined. 2a + 5 + 3a + 1 = 5a + 6.

25. A — 5y + 2
   Only like terms can be joined. 8y + 2 − 3y = 5y + 2.

26. B — 36 cm
   A square has four equal sides. 9 + 9 + 9 + 9 = 36.

27. D — 6 m 25 cm
   Change to centimetres: 345 + 280 = 625 cm = 6 m 25 cm.

28. C — 40
   5 × 8 = 40 squares.

29. B — 9 square units
   Area = 3 × 3 = 9 square units.

30. B — Put one on top of the other and see which one sticks out
   Placing one surface on the other shows which is bigger.

31. D — 125 blocks
   One layer has 5 × 5 = 25 blocks. There are 5 layers, so the volume is 25 × 5 = 125 blocks.

32. B — 80 crates
   5 × 4 = 20 crates per layer and 20 × 4 = 80 crates.

33. A — 7:45
   Each number on the clock face is worth 5 minutes. The minute hand at 9 shows 9 × 5 = 45 minutes, so the time is 7:45.

34. D — Ksh 12.50
   1,250 ÷ 100 = 12 remainder 50, so it is Ksh 12.50.

35. A — 50 cents
   One shilling is 100 cents, so half a shilling is 50 cents.

36. D — Ksh 195
   Cost = number × price = 3 × 65 = Ksh 195.

37. B — North
   Going clockwise the order is North, East, South, West. Going anticlockwise it is North, West, South, East. West followed by a quarter turn clockwise gives North.

38. D — A small square in the corner
   A right angle is marked with a small square.

39. A — 9
   10 − 1 = 9.

40. D — To check that the numbers are correct
   If the total does not match the number of items counted, we must count again.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: 6 m 25 cm
   Working / marking points: 345 + 280 = 625 cm (2 marks); 625 cm = 6 m 25 cm (1 mark).

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: 4 1/4 kg
   Working / marking points: Wholes 2 + 1 = 3 (1 mark); parts 2/4 + 3/4 = 5/4 = 1 1/4 (1 mark); total 4 1/4 kg (1 mark).

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: East
   Working / marking points: A half turn from north gives south (2 marks). A quarter turn anticlockwise from south gives east (2 marks).

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Yes. He has Ksh 660 left.
   Working / marking points: 2,000 is more than 1,340 (1 mark); 2,000 − 1,340 (1 mark); Ksh 660 (1 mark).

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: a and b are different, so 2a and 3b are not like terms and cannot be joined.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for unlike terms and 1 mark for the reason.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: A large sponge is light but a small stone is heavy. Mass depends on what the object is made of, so we must measure it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying size does not decide mass, 1 mark for an example, 1 mark for saying we must measure.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: 2,714
   Working / marking points: Ones 12 − 8 = 4 (1 mark); tens 2 − 1 = 1 (1 mark); hundreds 14 − 7 = 7 (1 mark); thousands 4 − 2 = 2 (1 mark).

48. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 7 hours 15 minutes (b) 4 hours 40 minutes (c) 1 hour 35 minutes
   Working / marking points: (a) 8:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. is 7 hours and then 15 minutes (2 marks); (b) 8:00 to 12:40 is 4 h 40 min (1 mark); (c) 1:40 p.m. to 3:15 p.m. is 1 h 35 min (2 marks).

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2 1/4 L
   Working / marking points: Change 4 L to 3 4/4 L (1 mark). 3 4/4 − 1 3/4 = 2 1/4 (1 mark). Check: 2 1/4 + 1 3/4 = 4 L (1 mark).

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: 3 1/2 L
   Working / marking points: 2 + 1 1/2 = 3 1/2. 1 mark for the addition and 1 mark for the unit.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: West
   Working / marking points: First turn east to south (1 mark); second turn south to west (1 mark); answer west (1 mark).

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 7.99, Ksh 8.05, Ksh 8.25, Ksh 8.50
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 7.99 first and 2 marks for the correct order of the rest.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: 9 m 20 cm
   Working / marking points: 230 × 4 = 920 cm (2 marks); 920 cm = 9 m 20 cm (1 mark).

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: 0.07, 0.57, 0.7, 0.75
   Working / marking points: Write with two decimal places: 0.70, 0.07, 0.75, 0.57. 1 mark for 0.07 first, 2 marks for the rest in order.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: Fold the rectangle so that the two halves match. There are two folds that work: along the middle from top to bottom and along the middle from side to side. So there are 2 lines of symmetry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for folding, 1 mark for halves matching, 1 mark for each of the two lines (or 2 marks for saying 2 with reasons).

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: 2 1/2 L
   Working / marking points: 5 − 2 1/2 = 2 1/2. 1 mark for the subtraction and 1 mark for the unit.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: 250, 500, 750, 1,000, 1,250. Rule: add 250.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the rule and 2 marks for correct numbers.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: 6 1/2 kg
   Working / marking points: 8 − 1 1/2 = 6 1/2. 1 mark for the subtraction and 1 mark for the unit.

59. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) mango 4, banana 3, orange 2, pawpaw 1 (total 10) (b) mango (c) 4 − 2 = 2 pupils
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for a correct table with title and headings, 1 mark for correct tallies and totals, 1 mark for (b), 1 mark for (c).
